(i) the Fermi-LAt data in the Galactic center region are consistent with the presence of a diffuse component associated with the interaction of the steady-state cosmic-ray sea, and (ii) the H.E.S.S.-LAT spectra of the diffuse Galactic emission can be explained by a CR radial distribution with a spectral index of ∼2.6.

(i) the bulk of the diffuse GR emission can be explained by the interaction with gas of the Galactic CR sea, and (ii) the residual emission can be explained as due to a radial-dependent component associated with a central CR accelerator.

the study of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and the related γ-ray diffuse emission.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fermi-Lat and HESS data are compatible with the presence of a large-scale CR sea, with a radial dependence of the diffusion coefficient, and with a central source.

the diffuse emission measured by HESS and Fermi in the GC region is not a signature of a central source, but it is rather due to the interaction between CRs and the gas of the central molecular zone, as it is the case for the GR emission.
the GC region is a source of γ-ray emission, but the GR is the main contributor of the diffuse emission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GC/GR γ-ray data can be explained in a consistent way by a single CR population, without the need of invoking a central source.
the GC region is dominated by a diffuse emission that is not necessarily associated with a pointlike source.
the diffuse γ-ray emission in the GC region can be naturally interpreted in the framework of a steady-state model for Galactic CRs.
